items.followUp: What is the scope of pharmaceutical chemistry?

rubric.why: Identifies industrial chemistry as a branch of chemistry.
rubric.description: Names industrial chemistry as a branch of chemistry.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as a branch of chemistry, especially applied chemistry.

rubric.why: States the scale and purpose of industrial chemistry.
rubric.description: Mentions the manufacture of chemicals or useful products on a large scale.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for referring to large-scale or commercial manufacture.

modelAnswer: Industrial chemistry is the branch of applied chemistry concerned with manufacturing chemicals and useful products on a large or commercial scale.

items.followUp: Name two elements that are gases at room temperature.

rubric.why: Mercury is one of the two elements that is liquid at room temperature.
Bromine is the other element that is liquid at room temperature.

modelAnswer: Mercury and bromine exist in the liquid state at room temperature.

items.followUp: How is cobalt-60 used in the treatment of cancer?

rubric.why: Identifies the radioactive isotope commonly used in radiotherapy.
rubric.description: Names cobalt-60 as the isotope used.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying cobalt-60 (or Co-60).

rubric.why: Explains how its radiation is used against cancer.
rubric.description: States that gamma radiation is directed at cancerous cells to destroy or kill them.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the use of gamma rays to destroy cancer cells.

modelAnswer: These rays are directed at cancerous cells to destroy them.

items.followUp: Define an orbital and state how it differs from a shell.

rubric.why: A shell is an electron energy level associated with the atom's nucleus.
rubric.description: Defines a shell as an energy level around the nucleus that contains electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a shell as an electron energy level around the nucleus.

rubric.why: A subshell is a subdivision within a shell.
rubric.description: Defines a subshell as a subdivision of a shell, containing orbitals of similar energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a subshell as a division or part of a shell.

modelAnswer: A shell is a principal energy level around the nucleus in which electrons are present.
A subshell is a subdivision of a shell containing orbitals of similar energy.

items.followUp: State the modern periodic law and name the scientist associated with it.

rubric.why: The law describes the recurring similarity in properties of every eighth element when arranged by atomic mass.
rubric.description: States the pattern of similar properties for every eighth element in the arrangement by increasing atomic mass.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the key every-eighth-element pattern.

rubric.why: John Newlands proposed the Law of Octaves.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct scientist.

modelAnswer: When elements are arranged in increasing order of their atomic masses, the properties of every eighth element are similar to those of the first, like notes in a musical octave.
This is the Law of Octaves, proposed by John Newlands.

items.followUp: Write two objectives that alchemists tried to achieve.

rubric.why: Transmuting base metals into gold was a major objective of alchemy.
rubric.description: States the aim of changing base metals into gold.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the transmutation-to-gold objective.

rubric.why: Alchemists also sought an elixir of life to extend life or cure diseases.
rubric.description: States the aim of finding the elixir of life, prolonging life, or curing diseases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one of these related objectives.

modelAnswer: Alchemists tried to change base metals into gold.
They also sought an elixir of life to prolong life or cure diseases.

items.followUp: Distinguish between a polar covalent bond and a non-polar covalent bond.

rubric.why: A lone pair remains associated with one atom rather than being shared in a bond.
rubric.description: Defines a lone pair as a non-bonding pair of electrons belonging to one atom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a lone pair is not shared between atoms.

rubric.why: A bond pair is shared by atoms to form a covalent bond.
rubric.description: Defines a bond pair as a pair of electrons shared between two atoms in a covalent bond.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a bond pair is shared to form a covalent bond.

modelAnswer: A lone pair is a pair of valence electrons belonging to one atom and not shared in a bond.
A bond pair is a pair of electrons shared between two atoms to form a covalent bond.

items.followUp: Why does sweating help to cool the body?

rubric.why: The faster, higher-energy molecules escape from the liquid during evaporation.
rubric.description: Explains that higher-energy molecules leave the liquid surface during evaporation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the escape of higher-energy molecules.

rubric.why: The remaining liquid has lower average kinetic energy and therefore becomes cooler.
rubric.description: Connects the loss of high-energy molecules with a lower temperature or cooling.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking evaporation to a decrease in the remaining liquid's temperature.

modelAnswer: During evaporation, molecules with higher kinetic energy escape from the liquid surface.
The average kinetic energy of the remaining molecules decreases, so the liquid's temperature falls and cooling occurs.
